text: Write a class that takes the current time as a parameter rather than reading the clock. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: static int due(___, int interval) {     // the day is supplied, not fetched
explanation: Verified: 3 then 13. A class that calls `LocalDate.now()` cannot be tested without waiting or installing a fake clock, and time is the single most common source of untestable code. Passing it in means every scenario — due tomorrow, overdue by a week, a leap day — is one line in a test. It is the same move as taking the `Scheduler` in the constructor: push the decision outward so the class depends on data rather than on the environment.
